#9819. This week: Git security fixes, agent skills, and running AI at scale

This week's stories circle one theme: making AI agents dependable in real engineering work. Git shipped security fixes you should install now. GitHub published its October availability report and a guide to portable agent skills. Martin Fowler's site contributed three pieces on glossaries, test contracts, and durable execution for long-running agents, plus notes on the new Technology Radar.

Git released updates addressing six security vulnerabilities. The affected areas include recursive clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports.

Because Git runs on virtually every developer machine and CI runner, these bugs expose a wide surface. A malicious repository could potentially trigger them during routine clone or merge operations.

Check which version your systems run and upgrade to the patched release. Pay attention to CI images and build agents, which teams update less often than workstations.

Source: Git security vulnerabilities announced

GitHub's monthly availability report covers eight incidents that degraded service performance during October.

These reports are worth more than a skim. They show which subsystems fail most often, and they help you decide how much redundancy your workflows need around GitHub-dependent automation.

If your pipeline assumes GitHub is always up, read the incident details and consider how your jobs behave during degraded performance, not just full outages.

Source: GitHub availability report: October 2026

GitHub published a practical guide to agent skills: files that capture repeatable engineering work so agents can review and reuse them. The key split is that skills travel, while tools, project context, and permissions stay specific to the host that runs the agent.

This separation matters if you support several agents or editors. You write the skill once instead of duplicating prompts and instructions per tool.

If your team keeps rebuilding the same prompts for common tasks, the guide is worth reading. Treat skills like code: version them and review changes.

Source: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills

Martin Fowler describes using an LLM to build a glossary of an organization's specialized terms, then feeding that glossary to any LLM working in that domain. The source material can be documents, emails, and chat logs; most organizations already generate enough text.

The interesting detail is that the generator should flag two things: terms new to the model, and familiar terms used in unfamiliar ways. The second category causes the most confusion, because the model confidently applies its default meaning.

If your team uses LLMs against internal systems or domain-specific processes, this is a cheap way to cut misinterpretation. Start with your existing documentation.

Matteo Vaccari argues that when AI writes both production and test code, developers become the code's customers. So customer tests, not developer tests, become the primary contract between humans and AI. Moving that contract into test data rather than test code makes it harder for a coding agent to quietly weaken it.

The economics changed too. Domain-specific language parsers and custom test runners used to be expensive to build and maintain. AI makes them cheap enough to justify.

If you review AI-generated code, ask what stops the agent from editing its own tests. Data-driven test definitions are one concrete answer.

Source: Tests as data: ensuring AI-generated code does what we want

The November Thoughtworks Technology Radar is out, heavy on AI blips from the last six months. Chris Ford's accompanying article covers the macro trends.

The sharpest point: a small enthusiastic team can make agents work because they share context, a budget, and a mental model, and review each other's output in person. Two hundred people cannot. At scale, new questions appear: how teams share context, what the token spend looks like, how to handle increased review load, what agents may read and change, and who owns the harness everyone depends on.

If you are moving from an agent pilot to a wider rollout, read the radar article and use those questions as your checklist.

Kiran Prakash explains durable execution, an emerging pattern for agents that run for days or weeks and interact with people and external systems. The runtime records the result of each step that touches the outside world. On failure, the program reruns, skips completed steps, and rebuilds its state from the record.

This addresses a real gap. A crash on day three of a week-long task should not mean starting over. The model resembles workflow engines, applied to agent loops.

If you build agents that outlive a single request, evaluate whether your runtime persists step results. Frameworks built on this idea are worth comparing before you write your own recovery logic.

Source: Long-horizon agents and durable execution

These write-ups are researched and published with no paywall, sponsor, or tracking. If one saved you an afternoon, a small tip keeps them coming.

#9816. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing.

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.

I use the paid versions of both Grammarly and Pro Writing Aid. Both of them have issues:- Grammarly IS more focused on nonfiction than fiction. If you're writing fiction, you may find Grammarly's insistence on "Conciseness" annoying. They seem to want to take the soul out of your writing, which is fine for a corporate report or technical manual, but not for your Great American Novel.- Grammarly pushes features on users that are not ready for prime time. It doesn't matter that you never agreed to be a beta tester for them; you get to do it anyway.- Pro Writing Aid actually counts the occurrences of words in your document and tells you when a word has been overused compared to published literature. Grammarly, on the other hand, seems hell-bent to remove certain words that it has deemed overused from the language, whether or not they're actually overused in your document.- Grammarly's Clarity function is simply horrible. It mangles sentences and changes their meaning. Sometimes the result of its suggestion is unintelligible garbage.- Grammarly allows you to turn off some checks, but not all of them. Unfortunately, the ones you cannot turn off are some of the most irritating (such as that horrible "Clarity"). On the other hand, Pro Writing Aid lets you choose which checks you use.- Pro Writing Aid has a mediocre command of American English (it's a British product). The app insists on rules of grammar and spelling that are outright wrong, per Merriam-Webster, the Chicago Manual of Style, and modern usage as shown by Google Books Ngram. At one point, Pro Writing Aid insisted that American English did not include the words "holiday" and "autumn," that "vacation" and "fall" must be used instead.- Pro Writing Aid's rules for commas are 100 percent consistent with the way I learned them in high school--50 years ago! They do not reflect modern usage. Grammarly is much better at this.- Pro Writing Aid seems to waste their limited resources on tweaking their UI. Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

#9814. GPT-4.5 Fooled 73% of Judges: 20 Turing Tests, Detectors and Fakes to Check Your AI Radar

Challenging us to question what it means to think.

Challenging us to question what it means to think.

Challenging us to question what it means to think.

In a 2025 UC San Diego study, people picked GPT-4.5 as the human 73% of the time, more often than they picked the actual humans. ELIZA, a 1960s chatbot, scored 23%, slightly ahead of GPT-4o without a persona at 21%. Here are 20 tests from the Turing Test directory where you can check whether you still tell human from machine across chat, text, faces, art, voice and video.

The Turing test used to be a thought experiment. Now it's a party game, a research method and a product category. Cameron Jones and Benjamin Bergen's three-party Turing test had 284 participants chat with a human and an AI at the same time and then pick the human. GPT-4.5 with a persona prompt won 73% of the time, and LLaMa-3.1-405B won 56%.

The public versions tell the same story. AI21 Labs' "Human or Not?" game ran more than 10 million conversations, and players guessed right only 68% of the time. They were worse at spotting the bots (60%) than at spotting the humans (73%). And it isn't just chat: in a blind listening study covered on HackerNoon, listeners trying to pick out AI-composed piano music were "essentially guessing," at close to 50% accuracy.

So test yourself. A note on what's included: not everything here is a quiz. Some are games, some are detectors that try to make the call for you, and some are the generators that make the fakes. To understand the Turing test in 2026, you need all three.

1. Human or Not? by AI21 Labs. You get a two-minute chat with a stranger, then guess whether it was a person or a bot. It became the largest Turing test ever run, with more than 1.5 million participants. The research paper breaks down the tricks players used to unmask bots.

2. Loebner Prize. This was the original Turing test competition, held from 1991 according to its Wikipedia history. It's no longer running; its last winner was Mitsuku in 2019. It belongs on any list because it shows how long "fooling the judges" was the goal, and how easy it looks now.

3. Bot or Not (Botometer) by Indiana University's OSoMe. It scores whether a social media account is a bot. It's a Turing test turned into a classifier. The live version shut down after X ended free researcher access, and the Botometer X archive only covers accounts created before June 2023.

4. GLTR (Giant Language model Test Room) from the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab and Harvard NLP. Paste text and it colors each word by how predictable it was to a language model. It was built in 2019 to spot AI-written text, and it's still the best way to see why AI text "feels" smooth.

5. GPTZero. This is the AI-writing detector that teachers made famous. Run your own writing through it to see how often humans get flagged. HackerNoon's guide on how to detect text generated by AI explains what these tools measure.

6. Poem or AI? You read a poem and decide who wrote it. The research on this is humbling: in Porter and Machery's Scientific Reports study, 1,634 readers couldn't reliably tell ChatGPT poems from famous poets', and they rated the AI poems higher.

7. NYT AI Article Quiz by The New York Times. Short passages, one question: human or AI?

8. WritersBrew AI Detector. A writing tool with a built-in check on whether a passage reads as machine-written.

9. Winograd Schema Challenge. This is the benchmark proposed as a better Turing test. Who does "it" refer to in "The trophy doesn't fit in the suitcase because it's too big"? It's easy for people. For years it was hard for machines.

10. Which Face Is Real? by Jevin West and Carl Bergstrom at the University of Washington. You see two faces and click the real one. It logged about 4 million plays in two weeks after its 2019 launch, and players were right about 70% of the time against StyleGAN fakes.

11. This Person Does Not Exist. This is the generator, not the quiz. Every refresh shows a face of someone who was never born. Look at the ears, teeth and backgrounds to learn the tells.

12. Sensity AI. A commercial deepfake detection platform for faces, video and identity fraud. It's what the professionals use when the stakes are higher than a game.

13. AI or Not. Upload an image and get a verdict on whether it's AI-generated. Try it on your own photos first.

14. Artbreeder. A collaborative image generator where you "breed" images by mixing them. Spend ten minutes making fakes and you'll get better at spotting them.

15. MIT GAN Dissect from MIT CSAIL. A research tool that shows which neurons inside a GAN draw trees, doors or clouds, and lets you switch them off. It doesn't test you. It shows you what's inside the machine you're testing.

16. Real or Fake Voice. Listen to clips and decide which are human speech and which are AI voice clones. This one matters most in practice, because voice cloning is the deepfake behind phone scams.

17. AIVA AI Music. An AI music composer. Play its tracks for friends without telling them and see who notices.

18. Deepfake Detection Challenge. The Kaggle competition, organized by Facebook with industry and academic partners, to build automatic deepfake detectors. Its dataset is still a standard for training them.

19. Detective (Deepware). Paste a video link and it scans for face manipulation.

20. FakeApp / Faceswap. The deepfake software that started it all. It's on this list because detectors are trained against it.

The pattern holds across formats. People do only somewhat better than a coin flip at spotting AI, and they get worse as models improve. Faces were about 70% in 2019, chat was 68% in 2023, and by 2025 people were choosing GPT-4.5 over real humans. The Turing test has stopped being a bar for machines to clear. It's turning into a skill humans have to practice.

Browse and filter every test by type (Audio, Classic, Game, Modern LLM, Social, Visual), difficulty and access in the Turing Test directory.

#9812. The History of 'Architecture Decision Record'

ADR = Architecture Decision Record，架构决策记录。一条 ADR 就是一个.md 文件，记录一个架构上重要的决定：当时什么处境、桌上摆了哪几个方案、为什么选了这个、为此认下了哪些副作用。

💡 关键在最后半句。ADR 不是“我们决定用 PostgreSQL”这句结论——结论不值钱，值钱的是“为什么不是 MongoDB、为什么不是留着 MySQL 加分片、我们明知道放弃什么”。只写结论的 ADR 是宣言，不是决策。

Nygard 原话里那个判定标准特别好用：影响结构、非功能特性、依赖、接口或构建方式的，才叫“架构显著”。反过来——一个 lint 规则、一个 bug fix、一次重命名，不配占一个 ADR 编号，commit message 就够了。

“ADR 库 / ADR catalog” 则是这些文件的集合 + 索引 + 模板 + 状态机 + 追踪关系的总和。它不是一个文件夹，是一套决策账本（decision log）：append-only、编号不复用、被推翻也不删、只在新 ADR 里 Supersedes: ADR-0003 指回去。

这个“只追加不改写”的性质，正是它能当 AI 架构师知识库地基的原因——任何一个时间点上，“当前生效的 ADR 集合”= 那份时点的架构意图快照，Git checkout 到那个 commit 就能复原当时团队脑子里在想什么。

Michael Nygard 2011-11-15 发在 Relevance（后归 Cognitect）博客上的原版，CC0 扔进公有领域，这是它能席卷全行业的隐藏原因——法务零摩擦。全部内容就五块：

四段各回答一个问题：标题=这是关于啥的、Status=走到哪一步了、Context=为什么是现在、Decision=到底干了啥（祈使句，“我们将用 X”而不是“我们考虑用 X”）、Consequences=变容易了什么、变难了什么。

⚠️ 90% 团队写废 ADR 都废在同一处：Consequences 只写好的不写坏的。而“我们明知道会变难的是什么”恰恰是三年后新人最想翻的那一栏。

Nygard 够轻，但多干系人、多方案选型时撑不住——没地方放“考虑过的选项”、没地方放“决策驱动因子”。Olaf Zimmermann（HSR OST，前 IBM 咨询架构师）带头搞了 MADR（Markdown Architectural Decision Records），把模板扩成这样：

一句话版：“在〈上下文〉下，面对〈关注点〉，我们选了〈方案〉，为拿到〈质量属性〉，接受〈副作用〉。” 适合 Slack 里当场拍板、事后补档的场景，一句顶一段。

📌 一条铁律：一个仓库里只许有一种格式。混着用比任何一种单用都糟——检索、模板、CI 校验全废。

MADR 官方推荐落法是 docs/decisions/，Nygard 原文写的是 doc/adr/，两者都是社区正统，挑一个别混：

命名约定就一条：NNNN-lowercase-with-dashes.md，NNNN 四位零填充、永不复用、按创建顺序不按主题分。为啥按顺序不按目录分类？因为 ADR 的价值一半在时间轴上——“第 3 号决定之后第 17 号为什么推翻它”这条线索，一分类就断了。分类交给 front matter 的 tags: 和 affects: 去做，别动文件名。

新手建完目录就冲去写 0001，跳过 README，三个月后库就烂了。README 至少回答六件事：

那句“CI 自动生成表格”是灵魂——手写索引必烂，机器生成的索引才活得过两次人员更替。

最后一行是 2025 年之后新增的一环，也是接回你上一个问题的关键，下面第五节专门讲。

这块比多数人想的有意思——ADR 不是 2011 年凭空蹦出来的，它是至少四波人接力做出来的。

软件架构作为一个正式学科在 1990 年代成型时，“记录设计背后的 why”就是核心议题。SEI 的 Bass / Clements / Kazman 在《Software Architecture in Practice》里就把“rationale（设计理由）”列为架构文档的一等公民；ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2011（架构描述国际标准）更是直接给了 ADR 的 9 个建议字段模板。

工业界更早。Olaf Zimmermann 考证：IBM Global Services Method 至少从 1998 年就有一个叫 ARC-100 – Architectural Decisions 的交付物，跟着每期项目走。同期 Philippe Kruchten 的 RAR（Rationale-based Architecture Reconstruction）、Antonio de Boer 的 Addressed / As-Is / To-Be 三段式都在各大咨询公司内流传。

那为什么没火？ 因为那时候的载体是 Word + Rational Rose + 共享盘，写一条理由要开一次变更控制委员会（CCB）。重量级到只有航天/银行核心敢用，互联网团队看一眼就跑了。

思想更上游还有一脉常被引用：Christopher Alexander 1977 年《A Pattern Language》——每个“模式”都是“上下文 + 力（forces）+ 解决 + 后果”的四段结构。GoF 设计模式抄了它的壳，Nygard 抄了它的骨。（这一条是社区通行的溯源说法，Nygard 原文没明写致敬，别当成他亲口认证。）

Michael Nygard——《Release It!》作者，当时在 Relevance（后并入 Cognitect）——发了 《Documenting Architecture Decisions》。全文没提 ISO、没提 IBM、没引一篇论文，就讲了一件被他反复看到的事：

重大架构决定是在会议室、走廊、Standup 间隙做出来的，只活在几个人的脑子里。半年后这人跳槽了，新人看着 MySQL 分库分表的怪异 schema 问“为啥不直接换 PG”，没人答得上来，于是团队要么盲从、要么重吵一遍。

为什么是 2011 年爆？ 三个时区同时到位：Git 已经赢了 SVN（“文档和代码同仓同 PR”第一次变得自然）、Markdown 刚被 GitHub 加冕、微服务运动开始让“一个系统一年做 50 个架构决定”成为常态。重量级文档扛不住这个频率，轻量级刚好卡在甜点。

范式 shift 一句话：以前 ADR 是“对下一个工程师的礼貌”，现在是编码代理每次会话都要加载的承重上下文。Claude Code 读 CLAUDE.md、Cursor 读 .cursor/rules、Copilot 读 .github/copilot-instructions.md——这些文件如果和 ADR 各写各的，三个月后必然互相打脸（Actual AI 的原话：“The same decision gets restated in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, a README, and a wiki page, and the four copies disagree within a few months.”）。

于是社区给出的新写法叫 agent-optimized ADR——同一条决策，人读一版，Agent 读一版，人那版编译出 Agent 那版：

⚠️ 这一代真正的难点不是“写”，是“防腐烂”。Anthropic 官方都在文档里念叨“记得定期 review 你的 CLAUDE.md 删掉过期条目”——几乎没有团队真做。所以 2026 年的最佳实践是：把 ADR 保鲜这件事本身交给一个 Agent，让它扫代码、对账、去重、解冲突、提 PR，人只做签字。

现在把两轮串起来。你上一轮问“灌完材料变成 AI 架构师”，光灌 PDF 和 Confluence 是不够的——那些材料里 60% 是“是什么”，只有 40% 是“为什么”，而架构师值钱的恰恰是那 40%。ADR 库就是把这 40% 提纯出来、结构化、可追溯后的产物。

💡 一句可以贴在墙上的话：“PDF 让 AI 架构师知道我们做过什么；ADR 库让它知道我们为什么做、放弃了什么、什么条件下该改主意。” 前者是百科，后者才是判断力。

#9809. A 23M-Parameter Model Still Wins: 338 Embedding Models Ranked by Real Downloads

We publish the best academic papers on rule-based techniques, LLMs, & the generation of text that resembles human text.

all-MiniLM-L6-v2, a 23M-parameter sentence-transformers model, was downloaded 177M times on Hugging Face in the last 30 days. That's 38% of all downloads across the 213 open-weight embedding models tracked by the TextModels directory, and more than the next four models combined. Below are all 338 embedding models in the directory: open weights ranked by downloads, then hosted APIs, Ollama builds and the historical models that started it all.

Most "best embedding model" lists rank by benchmark score, like PremAI's ranking by MTEB score, cost and self-hosting. Benchmarks tell you what's best on paper. Downloads tell you what developers actually ship, and the two lists look very different.

The sentence-transformers family's lead has a history. As HackerNoon's overview of embeddings for RAG puts it, "Simply said, the BERT model isn't the best for similarity search." SBERT fixed that by embedding each sentence separately so vectors can be computed once and compared fast, and its descendants still dominate the download charts.

Everything comes from the TextModels directory's Embedding filter (338 models) as of November 11, 2026. Hugging Face entries are ranked by 30-day downloads pulled from the Hugging Face API. "Verified" means the TextModels directory fetched and confirmed that model's metrics per model. Hosted API models have no public download counts, so they're grouped by provider, alphabetically. Some hosted entries, like OpenAI's 001-series search models, are long retired. They stay in the list because people still search for them when migrating old pipelines.

These are models you call over an API instead of downloading. The list covers current models and retired ones still found in old codebases.

248. textembedding-gecko-multilingual@001

Ollama doesn't publish download counts, so these are sorted from smallest to largest. Pick the smallest one that clears your quality bar.

285. qwen3-embedding 0.6b (Alibaba / Qwen)

288. nomic-embed-text-v2-moe latest (size not listed)

Before sentence-transformers there were word vectors, and before RAG there was semantic search. These are the ancestors of everything above.

289. word2vec Skip-gram Google News (Google)

297. GloVe Twitter 27B 200d (Stanford NLP)

298. GloVe Twitter 27B 100d (Stanford NLP)

299. GloVe Twitter 27B 50d (Stanford NLP)

300. GloVe Twitter 27B 25d (Stanford NLP)

301. fastText Common Crawl 300d 2M (Meta AI)

302. fastText Wiki News 300d 1M (Meta AI)

303. ELMo Original 5.5B (Allen Institute for AI)

305. Universal Sentence Encoder DAN (Google)

306. Universal Sentence Encoder Transformer (Google)

320. Sentence-BERT Base NLI Mean Tokens (UKP Lab)

321. Sentence-RoBERTa Large NLI STS-B (UKP Lab)

322. SimCSE BERT Base Supervised (Princeton)

323. SimCSE BERT Base Unsupervised (Princeton)

324. SimCSE RoBERTa Large Supervised (Princeton)

325. SimCSE RoBERTa Base Unsupervised (Princeton)

If you need a default today, the download data points to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 or bge-small-en-v1.5 for English, bge-m3 or multilingual-e5 for multilingual, and Qwen3-Embedding for top quality if you have the GPU. Then test on your own data. The model is only half the stack; HackerNoon's guide to choosing a vector database for a production RAG chatbot covers the other half.

To compare all 3,009 text models, including rerankers, classifiers and the LLMs these embeddings feed, browse the TextModels directory.

#9807. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

#9806. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9805. Copiar una base NoSQL no es exportar JSON: lo que aprendimos haciendo backups de Firestore

Autor: Carlos Jimenez Laura Curso: Base de Datos II · Universidad Privada de Tacna Actividad: Estrategias de copia de seguridad NoSQL, desarrollada junto con Arturo Cutipa Flores En PostgreSQL ejecutas pg_dump y obtienes un archivo que recrea la base. En Firestore, con el plan gratuito, no existe un equivalente: la exportación administrada exige un plan de pago y un bucket de Cloud Storage. La idea obvia es leer todos los documentos y guardarlos como JSON, y esa copia parece correcta hasta que intentas restaurarla. En este artículo cuento qué se pierde con esa idea y cómo lo resolvimos en StockSeguro, un inventario con copias automáticas, cifradas y comprobadas.

Enlaces del proyecto • Aplicación: https://stockseguro-firestore.onrender.com • Repositorio público: https://github.com/CRJL19/firestore-backups • Video: https://youtu.be/56mY6DRLr8U

Figura 1. StockSeguro con el panel de copias de seguridad.

Elegimos la copia lógica porque era lo posible con nuestro presupuesto, no porque sea la mejor en general. Para una base grande en producción, recomendaría la nativa.

Cuatro formas de perder datos sin enterarte

1. JSON no conoce los tipos de Firestore Un documento nuestro tiene un Timestamp, un GeoPoint y una referencia a su proveedor. JSON.stringify los convierte en objetos corrientes, y al restaurar ya no son esos tipos. La referencia deja de ser una referencia y ninguna consulta por fecha vuelve a funcionar.

Por eso cada tipo especial se guarda con una etiqueta:

Y hay una decisión deliberada al final de esa función: un tipo desconocido lanza un error. Prefiero que falle la copia a que parezca correcta y le falten datos.

2. Las subcolecciones no vienen con su padre Leer products no trae products/{id}/movements. Hay que recorrerlas. Y hay un caso peor: una subcolección puede colgar de un documento que ya no existe. Firestore lo llama documento fantasma, y un collection.get() no lo devuelve, así que sus hijos quedarían fuera. listDocuments() sí los incluye:

Una de nuestras pruebas crea justo ese caso, borra todo, restaura y comprueba que el hijo volvió.

3. Una copia que tarda no es una foto Si la app sigue escribiendo mientras copias, puedes guardar un producto de hace un minuto con los movimientos de ahora. Resolvimos esto leyendo los documentos dentro de una transacción de solo lectura, de modo que todo corresponde a un mismo instante:

4. Un borrado no deja rastro La copia incremental lee lo que cambió según updatedAt, pero un documento borrado ya no tiene ese campo: simplemente deja de existir, y la consulta no puede verlo. Sin más, al restaurar reaparecerían productos eliminados. Por eso la app deja una marca en la misma operación que borra:

La estrategia completa • Copia completa cada 7 días, que corrige cualquier desviación acumulada. • Copia incremental diaria, que gasta menos cuota porque lee menos documentos. • Restauración selectiva: --only products/abc123 recupera un producto y sus movimientos sin tocar el resto. • Cifrado AES-256-GCM, necesario porque los artifacts de un repositorio público se pueden descargar con cualquier cuenta de GitHub. • Objetivo de pérdida (RPO): 24 horas. El panel de la app avisa si la última copia supera las 26. Restaurar una incremental significa aplicar la cadena en orden: la completa y luego cada incremental. Dentro de cada copia, los borrados se aplican antes que los documentos, porque un documento presente en una copia existía al hacerla, aunque se hubiera borrado y creado de nuevo.

El problema que no se resuelve del todo La copia incremental depende de un contrato: todo se escribe a través de la app, con updatedAt y sus marcas de borrado. Alguien que borre un documento desde la consola de Firebase lo rompe, y la incremental no se entera. No pudimos evitarlo, pero sí detectarlo. Cada copia guarda los conteos reales del origen con consultas de agregación, que son baratas. Si al restaurar los números no coinciden, la verificación falla: products: la copia dice 1 y la restauración tiene 2 Una prueba automática reproduce ese caso. La solución entonces es una copia completa. Queda un hueco que prefiero admitir: una modificación externa que no cambie los conteos solo se recoge en la siguiente completa.

Cómo se publica y se automatiza El código está en un repositorio público de GitHub, y todo se ejecuta con GitHub Actions: • Cada git push ejecuta las 39 pruebas contra el emulador de Firestore, construye la imagen Docker y despliega en Render, un proveedor público en la nube. • Cada día, a las 03:00 hora de Perú, un workflow hace la copia, la restaura en un emulador y solo si coincide la guarda. Las copias se hacen con una cuenta de servicio de solo lectura, y la base está en Firestore, sobre Google Cloud.

Resultados En producción, con Firestore real, la primera copia completa dio esto:

Figura 2. Resumen de la copia verificada en GitHub Actions.

Después dejamos el workflow funcionando solo. Del 2 al 12 de noviembre se ejecutó todos los días y guardó 12 copias, todas verificadas antes de guardarse: 2 completas, la segunda creada automáticamente al cumplirse los 7 días, y 10 incrementales. Cada incremental cifrada pesa unos 650 bytes, frente a 1,8 KB de una completa. El simulacro de desastre lo hicimos en el emulador local, con los mismos comandos que usa GitHub Actions: una copia completa, un cambio de stock y un borrado, una incremental, la base vaciada y la restauración de la cadena. Volvieron los 25 documentos esperados en 237 ms, con el stock actualizado y sin el producto eliminado. En producción, la restauración existe como un workflow manual, pero no la ejecutamos para esta demostración. Un dato que me sorprendió: esa incremental, hecha segundos después de la completa, copió 26 registros frente a 27. No es un error. Cada incremental relee los últimos 5 minutos por seguridad, porque copiar de más es inofensivo y copiar de menos no lo es. El ahorro aparece cuando las copias están separadas por horas.

Limitaciones • Dos ubicaciones, no tres. Hay datos en Firestore y copias en GitHub. La regla 3-2-1 pediría una tercera. • Enteros y decimales. El SDK de JavaScript no distingue 1 de 1.0. Tampoco se conservan createTime ni updateTime, que asigna el servidor. • Memoria. Cada copia se procesa completa en memoria, adecuado para miles de documentos, no para millones. • La clave de cifrado. Si se pierde, las copias no sirven de nada, así que hay que guardarla también fuera de GitHub.

Qué me llevo En una base relacional el esquema y la herramienta de volcado resuelven casi todo por ti. En NoSQL, el esquema vive en la aplicación, y por eso la estrategia de copia también: tuvimos que cambiar cómo borra la app para poder copiar bien. Lo otro que me llevo es desconfiar de una copia hasta verla restaurada. Mi compañero Arturo cuenta en su artículo cómo automatizamos esa comprobación.

PaddleOCR (92.6K stars) beats MinerU (83.5K) and Tesseract (77.5K) as the most-starred open source OCR project on GitHub. Below are all 138 OCR and document-parsing repos with 1,000+ stars in the Text Mining directory, ranked.

Every RAG pipeline eventually hits the same wall: the PDF. Before a language model can answer anything about your contracts, papers or invoices, something has to turn pixels and layout into clean text. The tools for that job are splitting into two camps. In HackerNoon's comparison of OCR and vision LLMs, template-based OCR breaks when layouts shift, while vision LLMs read documents more flexibly but cost more at volume. The author's verdict: "It could mostly be a hybrid approach."

Meanwhile, the vision models are shrinking. Xiaomi-OCR-0 handles text, tables and formulas with 0.8B parameters, and TeleOCR does structured document parsing with 1.2B. This list is the "show me everything" version of that landscape.

The Text Mining directory tracks the 3,141 most-starred open source text mining projects on GitHub (100+ stars, no forks or archived repos). Its OCR & Documents filter tags 321 of them, which together hold about 1.24M stars. We kept repos with 1,000+ stars (161) and removed 23 that are tagged OCR but aren't really OCR or document tools: generic AI course repos, an inference framework, a clipboard syncer, and captcha solvers, which we chose not to promote. That leaves 138. Star counts are from the directory's November 11, 2026 snapshot.

A few patterns stand out in the full category:

The long tail (100 to 999 stars) is where you find niche tools like single-language engines, receipt parsers and research code. Browse all 321 on the OCR & Documents filter, or narrow by language, license and last-updated date.

#9799. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9792. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers

Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

#9785. AI Is Dividing Product Designers: Exploring vs. Building

Design Engineer at Matter Labs (creators of ZKsync and Prividium). Creator of DecentWealth, ScrollChess, and a few other apps.

Design Engineer at Matter Labs (creators of ZKsync and Prividium). Creator of DecentWealth, ScrollChess, and a few other apps.

Design Engineer at Matter Labs (creators of ZKsync and Prividium). Creator of DecentWealth, ScrollChess, and a few other apps.

A week ago, I attended PUSH UX in Munich, Europe's largest conference on product design and user experience, featuring speakers from Anthropic, Wise, Google, IKEA, n8n, and other prominent organizations. On my way home, I kept thinking about one recurring theme: product design teams are approaching AI from fundamentally different perspectives.

Some are cautiously experimenting with AI while trying to fit it into established processes. Others have already integrated it into their daily workflows, connecting research, prototyping, design, and code with fewer handoffs. The difference goes beyond tool adoption. It reflects how teams understand their work, organize collaboration, and measure product value.

Paulo Oliveira from IKEA highlighted a fundamental problem with the way organizations approach AI:

"Most efforts start with tools, copilots, and automation, and mistake faster cycles for value. The result is a pile of pilots nobody adopted, and a lot of people wondering what happened to the work they were good at. The alternative: to build something that fits, lasts, and makes an organization better at what it already does well. That starts by refusing the AI first, AI everything instinct."

I think this captures one of the central challenges in product design today.

Adding AI to an existing workflow can make individual tasks faster without improving the product or the way a team operates. Organizations can accumulate tools and experiments while leaving the underlying processes unchanged.

Meaningful adoption starts with understanding where teams lose time, which handoffs create friction, and where AI can improve how products are researched, designed, built, and validated.

For years, product design and software development operated as distinct stages. Designers worked in Figma, documented interactions, prepared specifications, and handed their work to engineers for implementation. This division made sense when building and testing functional interfaces required substantial engineering resources. AI-assisted development is changing that relationship.

After years of designing fintech and blockchain-based products, I kept encountering the same limitation: I could design an experience without having full control over how it was implemented.

About a year ago, I started building websites and applications from scratch with AI tools. As I described in my previous HackerNoon article, Claude Code Finally Made Me an Engineer After 10 Years in Figma, my workflow shifted from almost entirely Figma to roughly 90% Claude Code.

Working closer to production code lets me build, test, and iterate on interfaces directly, with fewer handoffs between design and engineering.

For product teams, this opens up several possibilities:

This doesn't mean every designer needs to become a full-time software engineer. Deep specialization remains essential, particularly in complex products. However, designers can work closer to implementation and contribute beyond the traditional boundaries of their roles.

Another exciting development is how AI is changing prototyping. Think about how difficult it used to be to create an interactive prototype for a specific device, such as an Apple Watch or an in-car infotainment system. Even without writing production code, designers can now use AI to build interactive prototypes tailored to specific hardware and explore how their ideas work in real-world contexts.

As AI makes prototyping, coding, and exploring alternatives easier, the focus of design work is shifting toward decision-making and product quality. Understanding whether it solves the right problem, meets user needs, and works reliably requires experience and critical judgment.

This is where faster workflows can create lasting value. Teams have more opportunities to test assumptions, explore alternatives, and identify problems before committing significant resources to a solution. However, individual productivity gains aren't enough. Organizations need to connect design, engineering, and product teams around shared workflows, clear quality standards, and meaningful evaluation of AI-generated output.

I'm particularly interested in how this can shape an AI-first product culture. The goal is to encourage experimentation while maintaining the technical rigor, security, and reliability that deep tech products demand.

Many designers argue that AI-generated product experiences lack quality. Are they right? Sometimes. Can the results improve? Absolutely.

AI-assisted research and discovery can produce shallow or generic results, especially when designers rely on AI without applying their own expertise and critical judgment. The quality of the outcome depends on how thoughtfully people guide, evaluate, and refine the process. Julia Bastian from Alasco explored this challenge in a session on AI discovery slop, examining how to recognize and address low-quality AI-generated research and insights.

The PUSH UX conference reinforced how differently the design community is responding to AI. Some teams are still finding their footing, while others are already changing how they work. My own experience has made me more comfortable working across design, product strategy, and engineering, but every team will need to find its own approach.

The important shift is to reconsider established workflows, explore where new capabilities can make a difference, and take greater ownership of business outcomes.

In this article, we explore the top 10 AI tools that are driving innovation and efficiency in various industries. These tools are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The tools included in our list are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for a variety of applications. Some of the tools focus on natural language processing, such as ChatGPT and Grammarly, while others focus on image and video generation, such as DALL-E and Lumen5. Other tools such as OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI,, and Surfer SEO are designed to help with specific tasks such as code understanding content writing and website optimization. ChatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect.

Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations.

DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use.

Overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is important to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data.

Overall, TabNine is a useful tool for developers that can help improve coding efficiency and reduce the time spent on writing code. #9773. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.

Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.

You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.

The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)

“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”

“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.

“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”

That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.

If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.

But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”

“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”

In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”

#9768. What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.

This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.

Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.

Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).

Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.

Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.

In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!

I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.

While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.

Find puerquitos and many more Mexican sweets in our feature celebrating pan dulce.

#9762. 16 pumpkin recipes, from cakes and cookies to bars and bread: We've got a marbled pumpkin cake, chewy pumpkin cookies, and even pumpkin milk bread.

It’s that time of year when pumpkin spice everything starts appearing on store shelves — candles, lip balm, air fresheners, beer, and of course, the ubiquitous PSL (pumpkin spice latte). That means fall is here, and more importantly, that pumpkin should make a grand return to your kitchen! Pull out your canned pumpkin — or better yet, make your own pumpkin purée — and stock your pantry with pumpkin pie spice, because we have the best pumpkin recipes to bake this fall.

This Pumpkin Swirl Cake takes my breath away every time I unmold it from its intricate loaf pan. The anticipation keeps building until I slice into the pound cake-like loaf and reveal the swirled pattern inside, marbled with both vanilla and spiced pumpkin batter. (Don’t fret if you don’t have the specialty loaf pan — this can also be baked in a standard loaf pan and adorned with a simple confectioners’ sugar icing.)

To make this recipe, you'll need: Patch O Pumpkins Loaf Pan and Pure Vanilla Plus

To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Sparkling Sugar

A cousin of Belgian-style Liège waffles, these Pumpkin Sugar Crunch Waffles have caramelized edges and a pleasant chew that’s reminiscent of brioche. The yeasted batter has pumpkin in it for flavor and color, plus Swedish pearl sugar that melts into pockets of crispy sugar. The best part? The batter rests overnight, so if you prepare it the night ahead, all you have to do the next morning is scoop and cook the batter for hot, crispy waffles in just a few minutes.

Get the recipe: Pumpkin Sugar Crunch Waffles

To make this recipe, you'll need: Swedish Pearl Sugar

I used to make the same pumpkin pie recipe for years, and it always left me wanting a little more excitement. Then I found this Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie and never looked back! The generously spiced filling uses nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and Vietnamese cinnamon to create a more flavorful pie than traditional versions. The secret to its silky-smooth texture? Corn syrup, which is an invert sugar and keeps the custard from becoming grainy. Substitute another invert sugar like honey or maple syrup if you like; I use maple syrup.

Get the recipe: Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon, Ginger, and Nutmeg

Whenever I have these tender, golden scones on hand, I look forward to getting out of bed the next morning because I know they’re waiting for me. They can be easily customized to use a range of mix-ins, depending on what you have in your pantry. My personal preference is a mix of crystallized ginger and Cinnamon Sweet Bits.

Get the recipe: Harvest Pumpkin Scones (or Gluten-Free Pumpkin Scones)

To make this recipe, you'll need: Mini Diced Ginger and Cinnamon Sweet Bits

If you’re looking for a way to make your whole kitchen smell like fall, these one-bowl, easy pumpkin muffins deliver — and fast. They’re ready in under an hour, so you can spend less time measuring, mixing, and cleaning and more time tackling your autumn bucket list.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Standard Muffin Pan

Making banana bread is an almost weekly activity in my house — except during fall, when we pivot to pumpkin bread instead. This is a quick, easy bake that satisfies my craving for something pumpkin-y, and it uses a simple trick to concentrate the pumpkin flavor and ensure the loaf is perfectly textured: The pumpkin purée is reduced on the stovetop to cook off excess moisture. (The process is similar to browning butter.) As a result, the final loaf is packed with pumpkin flavor.

Get the recipe: The Most Pumpkin Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Bread

To make this recipe, you'll need: Ginger and Semisweet Chocolate Chips

The buttery, brown sugar crust gets pressed into the pan (no rolling out pie dough!), and the silky pumpkin filling comes together with just a handful of ingredients. The (optional but highly recommended) sour cream whipped topping brings a slight tanginess and completes the traditional pumpkin pie experience.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice

This Pumpkin Milk Bread is exceptionally soft, squishy, and feather-light, while also packing in a lot of pumpkin. Pumpkin can often weigh down baked goods, but here the combination of a tangzhong, bread flour, and a long mix makes this bread simultaneously moist and high-rising.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant Yeast

This tender pumpkin crumb cake is for people who double the chocolate chips in pumpkin bread and the streusel on coffee cake. Atop the thin layer of spiced pumpkin cake lays a heavy blanket of buttery crumbs with a bold chocolate flavor, thanks to Dutch-processed cocoa powder.

Get the recipe: Pumpkin Cream Cheese Danish

To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk

To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice

Get the recipe: Pumpkin Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting

To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Offset Spatula

The pumpkin spice recipe I’m most excited to bake this fall is a mash-up of greats: Part-coffee cake, part-Bundt cake, part-pumpkin bread, this Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake deserves a category all of its own. It has two layers of espresso swirl tucked within a moist, spiced cake. Make it in your favorite Bundt pan or serve it as a loaf if you’re more of simple-is-better person. Either way, it’s great for snacking all day long.
